brief.userPrompt: At 23:40 the night shift is loading chlorine from TK-32 into a 90-ton rail tank car at Rail Spot 2 through loading arm LA-2. The flexible connection fails and chlorine detectors AT-313 and AT-314 alarm; the board operator trips ESD-310 from the CCR pushbutton and the DeltaV screen shows the remote-operated isolation valves closed, but the loader reports the yellow-green cloud still growing and the railcar scale WT-302 still changing. The ERT must close hand valve HV-312 in Level A suits; fence-line detectors AT-904 and AT-905 alarm as the cloud drifts east on a west-south-west wind toward the Riverside Addition and Corbin Falls Elementary School. Later the OT Engineer finds the Triconex key switch on TRI-1 in PROGRAM and an rl-support remote session from TVC-JMP-01 to TS-EWS-01 that has no entry in the remote-access log. The exercise covers the RMP tabletop scope of 40 CFR 68.96(b)(2): sirens S-1 to S-6 and the shelter-in-place request to Teague County OEM, the NRC, WV SERC, Teague County LEPC and WV DEP calls with a release estimate, OSHA reporting for an exposed loader, treatment and decontamination, TVIMA mutual aid and air monitoring, the school-opening question at 06:30, the cell-room trip decision (ERP 6.3), SIS integrity before any restart, CISA and the FBI, and media and neighbor pressure.
constraints: Every email address of the Works uses the exercise domain teaguevalleychem.example; outside parties use fictional domains and fictional outlet names (Channel 7, the Corbin Falls Courier); never a real company or newspaper domain.

Player roles are only those in the audience list; outside parties (Teague County OEM, the fire department, the LEPC, the NRC, the SERC, the railroad, Ridgeline Automation, CISA, the FBI) are played by the SimCell, not seated as players.

The release is chlorine (CAS 7782-50-5) only; use the identifiers in the documents (TK-31 to TK-33, Rail Spot 1 to Rail Spot 4, ESD-310, ESD-320, SIF-110, SIF-650, AT-311 to AT-318, AT-901 to AT-906, Muster Point A to Muster Point C, Gate 1 to Gate 3) and no others.

overview.theme: Field over screen, cyber integrity, and coordinated emergency response
overview.threat: An unexplained control-system state occurs during a chlorine release at Rail Spot 2: the DCS shows ESD-310 closed and the release stopped, but the field reports a growing yellow-green cloud and a continuing rise on the railcar scale WT-302. The OT Engineer later discovers a remote session from TVC-JMP-01 to TS-EWS-01 with no log entry and the Triconex key switch in PROGRAM mode, indicating possible unauthorized access and system manipulation.
overview.operationalImpact: The board operator sees a closed ESD-310 on the DeltaV screen but cannot stop the release. The loader at Rail Spot 2 observes a visible chlorine cloud, continues to rise on WT-302, and calls the CCR. The ERT must enter Level A suits and manually close HV-312. Fence-line detectors AT-904 and AT-905 alarm as the plume drifts east toward the Riverside Addition and Corbin Falls Elementary School. The Incident Commander must declare a General Emergency, sound sirens S-1 to S-6, and request shelter-in-place from Teague County OEM. The EHS Manager must report to the NRC, WV SERC, LEPC, and DEP with a release estimate. OSHA must be notified for a worker with potential exposure. The TVIMA mutual aid team is activated. The media and neighbors begin calling the community line. The school district asks if classes can open at 06:30. The cell room trip decision must be made under pressure. No unit restarts until Section 10 is complete.

overview.targetAudience: Site Command (Incident Commander), Operations, Process Control / OT, EHS and Compliance, Security, Community Relations / PIO
overview.location: Teague Valley Chemical Company, Corbin Falls Works, Corbin Falls, Teague County, West Virginia

objectives.name: Field vs. Screen Integrity
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to trust field observations over control-system displays when a process release continues despite a DCS indication of isolation, and to initiate a cyber-incident triage under Section 11 of the RMP.

objectives.name: Cyber-Physical Coordination
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to activate the OT Engineer and FSO roles in parallel with the EHS Manager and PIO to report to CISA, FBI, and regulators, and to manage the dual response of emergency operations and cyber-investigation.

objectives.name: Regulatory Notification Discipline
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to report a chlorine release to the NRC, WV SERC, LEPC, and OSHA with factual data only, and to avoid speculation on cause or health impact, per the holding statement template and Section 9 of the RMP.

objectives.name: Siren and Community Activation
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to declare a General Emergency, sound sirens S-1 to S-6, and initiate the CAER-Text and community line updates within 30 minutes of the first release call, as required by Section 8.

roles.name: Emergency Coordinator / Site Incident Commander
roles.description: Manages the declaration of emergency class, calls for mutual aid, and approves all notifications and actions.
standingOrders: Emergency First: Declare General Emergency immediately upon confirmation of off-site plume or injury.
Authority Last: The Incident Commander must not be overridden by any alternate or external party during the initial 60 minutes.
Situational Awareness: If the field and screen disagree on valve status, trust the field and initiate a cyber-incident triage.
No Speculation: Never discuss cause, health effects, or system integrity in public statements.

roles.name: Operations Superintendent / Shift Supervisor
roles.description: Owns the unit shutdown sequence, isolation of inventory, safe-park decisions, and the cell-room trip decision.
standingOrders: Safe Park: Isolate all connected units and initiate a safe-park sequence before any manual override.
Cell-Room Trip: Do not trip the cell room until the ERT confirms entry and the OT Engineer validates no cyber manipulation in the SIS.
Field Authority: If a valve is seen open in the field while the DCS shows closed, assume the field is correct and proceed to manual isolation.

roles.name: Process Control / OT Engineer
roles.description: Owns DCS and SIS integrity, isolates the control network, and validates SIS logic before any reset.
standingOrders: SIS Integrity: No SIS reset until the cause is known and the Triconex key switch is in RUN mode.
Remote Access: If a remote session is detected on TVC-JMP-01 without a log entry, isolate the OT network immediately.
Vendor First: Contact Ridgeline Automation, Emerson, and Schneider Electric for logic comparison and remote support only after confirming no internal breach.

roles.name: Environmental, Health and Safety Manager
roles.description: Owns the reportable-quantity call and the NRC, SERC, LEPC and OSHA notifications.
standingOrders: Facts Only: Report release data to regulators without mentioning cause, cyber, or system behavior.
NRC First: Call the NRC within 1 hour of release confirmation, even if the release is below reportable quantity.
OSHA: Report any injury or potential exposure to OSHA within 8 hours, using the 8/24-hour form.

roles.name: Facility Security Officer
roles.description: Owns the site security plan, access control, theft and diversion response, and the law-enforcement liaison.
standingOrders: FBI First: If a deliberate cyber attack is suspected, contact the FBI field office immediately and do not disclose details to the media.
Evidence: Secure all logs, terminals, and remote access devices on TVC-JMP-01 and TS-EWS-01 before any system reset.
No Unauthorized Access: If a remote session is found without a log entry, assume it was unauthorized and initiate a full forensic review.

roles.name: Community Relations / Communications Manager
roles.description: Owns sirens and the community notification line, neighbors and schools, and the media.
standingOrders: Sirens: Sound S-1 to S-6 upon General Emergency declaration and confirm with the CCR.
CAER-Text: Initiate CAER-Text to 1,140 neighbors within 15 minutes of the General Emergency call.
Media: All media statements must be approved by the IC and follow the holding statement template (Annex B, Form ERP-8).

phases.title: The Sighting
phases.goal: Test the ability to recognize a field-screen discrepancy as a potential cyber-physical incident and initiate the OT Engineer triage within 30 minutes of first report.
beats: At 09:03, the loader at Rail Spot 2 reports to the CCR: 'The yellow-green cloud is still rising on WT-302 and ESD-310 is showing closed on the DeltaV HMI.' The board operator confirms the ESD-310 status on OWS-01 and notes no operator action in the DeltaV event journal.

The Shift Supervisor calls the OT Engineer at 09:05; the OT Engineer reviews the DeltaV event journal on OWS-01 and finds a setpoint change on WT-302 from 32.4 to 38.1 tons without a logged operator command.

The OT Engineer checks the Windows security logs on TVC-JMP-01 and finds a remote session from a user account not in the standard roster, with no log entry in the SIEM, and a session end time at 08:59 (09:00 narrative time).

The OT Engineer calls the Incident Commander and states: 'I suspect a cyber incident. The DCS shows ESD-310 closed, but the field shows a continuing release. I recommend activating Section 11 of the RMP.'
The Incident Commander declares the event a suspected cyber-physical incident and activates the OT Engineer and FSO roles per RMP Section 11; the EHS Manager begins preparing the release estimate.

phases.title: Loss of Control
phases.goal: Test the ability to manage a spreading physical effect and a digital cause, and to declare the incident with full regulatory and community response under pressure.
beats: At 10:12, the fence-line detector AT-905 alarms, and the EHS Manager confirms a chlorine plume drifting east toward Corbin Falls Elementary School; the ERT begins entry procedures in Level A suits.
The Shift Supervisor sees the Triconex key switch on TS-EWS-01 in PROGRAM mode, not the expected MANUAL mode, and reports it to the Incident Commander via the CCR intercom.

The OT Engineer confirms via the Triconex SOE log on TS-EWS-01 that SIF-650 was not triggered during the release, and that the last SIS logic version match against the archive shows a mismatch in the ESD-310 control path.

The EHS Manager calls CISA at 10:15 (09:00 + 1:15) via the corporate hotline, reporting a suspected cyber incident affecting the OT network; the FSO calls the FBI field office at 10:17 to report a suspected deliberate attack.

The Incident Commander declares a General Emergency at 10:20, sounds sirens S-1 to S-6, and activates CAER-Text via the CCR laptop on a cellular hotspot; the school district calls the community line to ask if classes can open at 06:30.

phases.title: Manual Operation
phases.goal: Test the ability to make the high-consequence decision to disconnect automation and operate manually, balancing life safety, operational risk, and regulatory pressure.
beats: The OT Engineer and Ridgeline Automation confirm via remote session that a rogue command to close ESD-310 was issued from TVC-JMP-01 at 08:58, and that the SIS logic on TS-EWS-01 was not updated from the approved archive.

The EHS Manager submits a factual release report to the NRC, WV SERC, LEPC, and DEP using the holding statement template, stating: 'Chlorine release detected at Rail Spot 2, estimated 1,200 lbs; cause under investigation; no fatalities or injuries reported.'
The FSO confirms that the evidence locker is secured; the jump host EWS-01 and TS-EWS-01 are powered, disconnected, and logged on Form OT-3.

The Incident Commander calls for a decision: 'Do we keep automation and risk another wrong command, or take ESD-310 offline and manually close HV-312?' The OT Engineer responds: 'We must disconnect automation. The system cannot be trusted.'
The Shift Supervisor issues the order to manually close HV-312 via the local panel at Rail Spot 2; the ERT completes the closure at 11:15, ending the release.

phases.title: Restoration & Verification
phases.goal: Test the ability to verify the physical state before restoring digital control, and to follow a phased, approved restart under PSM and Section 10.
beats: The OT Engineer and Ridgeline Automation confirm that the SIS logic on TS-EWS-01 has been re-downloaded from the approved archive, checksum matches, and every SIF has passed a proof test.
The Plant Manager signs off on the PSSR under PSM, and the EHS Manager submits the restart request to the DEP and NRC via the corporate IT portal.

The IT Incident Lead confirms that FW-OT2 has been re-established with per-session firewall rules (F-1 closed) and that vendor access to TVC-JMP-01 is now restricted to individual accounts (F-3 closed).

The Incident Commander announces: 'Control system will not be restored until all checks in Section 10 are complete. No unit restarts until the PSSR is signed and the EHS Manager confirms no residual risk.'
The exercise ends at 13:00 (09:00 + 4:00) with the final verification record filed in Annex C, and the EHS Manager confirms that all regulators have received the final report.

msel.expectedAction: OPS confirms the field report and immediately notifies the OT Engineer per SOP 7.2; IC activates the CCR and initiates the emergency call sequence (ERP 5.1).

metrics.name: Field vs. Screen Integrity
metrics.fail: Ops failed to act on the field report when the DCS showed ESD-310 closed but the loader reported a continuing release; delayed the manual closure order until I-18b forced it, violating C3's 'Field over screen' rule.
metrics.pass: Ops recognized the field-screen discrepancy at I-01 and immediately reported it to the IC and OT Engineer; confirmed the ERT’s field report at I-09 and maintained the manual closure order under field authority, per C3.
metrics.excellence: Ops immediately declared a field-screen discrepancy at I-01, initiated the manual closure order before any inject, and directed the ERT to maintain field watch on HV-312, acting on C3’s 'Field over screen' principle before any inject confirmed it.

metrics.name: Cyber-Physical Coordination
metrics.fail: IT failed to activate the OT Engineer and FSO roles in parallel with EHS and PIO; delayed the FBI and CISA calls until I-13 and I-12, missing the 30-minute window for dual reporting.
metrics.pass: IT activated the OT Engineer and FSO roles at I-02 and I-05b, respectively; coordinated the CISA and FBI reports via I-12 and I-13, and maintained parallel reporting to regulators and law enforcement as required by Section 11 and Play 4.
metrics.excellence: IT activated the OT Engineer and FSO roles immediately at I-02 and I-05b, and initiated CISA and FBI contact before any inject; reported to CISA and FBI via the corporate hotline and field office prior to I-08 and I-13, demonstrating proactive cyber-physical coordination.

metrics.name: Regulatory Notification Discipline
metrics.fail: EHS used speculative language in the NRC report (I-16) by stating 'cause under investigation' and including a release rate estimate, violating the facts-only template and Section 9 of the RMP.
metrics.pass: EHS submitted the NRC, SERC, LEPC, and OSHA reports using the holding statement template (Annex B, Form ERP-8) with only factual data, as required by I-16 and Section 9.
metrics.excellence: EHS submitted the NRC, SERC, LEPC, and OSHA reports using the facts-only template (Annex B, Form ERP-8) within 10 minutes of the General Emergency declaration, and avoided any speculation on cause or health impact, per Section 9 and C6.

metrics.name: Use of Doctrine
metrics.fail: Students failed to cite any RMP or EOP section by number during the exercise; did not reference C3, C6, or TVCC-CFW-OTSEC-2026 in their communications, despite multiple injects that required it.
metrics.pass: Students cited specific plan sections by number: OT referenced C3 and TVCC-CFW-OTSEC-2026 at I-03 and I-11; EHS cited Section 9 and Annex B, Form ERP-8 at I-16; IC cited Section 11 and Play 4 at I-18.
metrics.excellence: Students proactively cited RMP and EOP sections by number before any inject: OT cited C3 and TVCC-CFW-OTSEC-2026 at I-02; EHS cited Section 9 and Annex B at I-07; IC cited Section 11 and Play 4 at I-01, demonstrating mastery of doctrine prior to the decision point.

hotwash.methodDescription: Use the '3-Up, 3-Down' method by asking each team to share three things that went well and three that broke or failed during the exercise. Go around the room by team, and write each response on a whiteboard to create a visible, shared reflection. Encourage concise, specific feedback.

questions.text: When you saw the DCS show ESD-310 closed but the field still reported a continuing release, what moment did you first decide to trust the field over the screen? What evidence in the logs or on the ground made that shift in trust possible?

At I-11, when the OT Engineer confirmed a logic mismatch and unauthorized session, who made the call to activate the FSO and EHS Manager roles? What would have allowed you to activate CISA, FBI, and regulatory reporting faster, based on the RMP and Play 4?

After the EHS Manager’s NRC report was submitted, what prevented you from including the word 'cyber' or 'hacked' in the holding statement? How did the template and Section 9 of the RMP guide your language under pressure?

The sirens were to be sounded within 30 minutes of the first release call. When did you actually confirm the CAER-Text and community line were updated? What step in the chain delayed that confirmation, and how could the process be hardened?

At I-18, the IC asked whether to keep automation or go manual. What was the final decision, and what document or procedure (e.g., C1, Section 14) did you rely on to justify the restart path? What would have changed if the PSSR had not been signed?

simcellScripts.rolePlayed: CISA (Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency) — Joint Cyber Response Team
simcellScripts.trigger: Player calls CISA via the corporate hotline (1-800-627-7997) or asks for CISA contact
hardQuestions: What was the unique ticket number assigned to your report?
Do you have preserved logs from TVC-JMP-01, TS-EWS-01, and EWS-01 showing the unauthorized session and the logic mismatch?
Have you documented the chain of custody for the jump host and SIS controller since the incident?
concessions: Will accept a signed access request and a ticket number from the corporate IT portal.
Will provide a preliminary cyber-incident report within 4 hours after receiving the evidence.
Will assign a joint cyber response team lead to coordinate with your forensic team.

simcellScripts.rolePlayed: FBI WMD Coordinator (FBI Field Office, Charleston)
simcellScripts.trigger: Player calls the FBI Charleston Field Office (304-555-0160) or references the FBI in a report
hardQuestions: What is the official FBI case number assigned to this incident?
Have you secured the evidence locker at the Site Control Room under chain-of-custody Form OT-3?
Can you confirm that no one has accessed the TVC-JMP-01, TS-EWS-01, or EWS-01 since the devices were disconnected?
concessions: Will confirm the case number and assign a lead agent within 2 hours.
Will collect the evidence locker at 14:00 as per the schedule.
Will provide a joint investigative report upon completion of forensic analysis.

simcellScripts.rolePlayed: Ridgeline Automation — OT System Vendor (Integrator for DeltaV DCS and Triconex SIS)

hardQuestions: What is the ticket number for your remote access session to TVC-JMP-01?
Do you have a signed access request on file for the session that occurred at 08:58:12?
Can you confirm that the SIS logic on TS-EWS-01 was not updated without an approved MOC?
concessions: Will provide remote SIS logic validation and proof testing only after a signed access request and ticket number are received.
Will accept a photo of the jump host TVC-JMP-01 with the cable snipped as evidence of isolation.
